elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New Subparagraph 21.3: "each Party's aggregate liability to each other Party arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed..." — the cap is expressed symmetrically for every Party, including us and the counterparties.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 21.3 caps at "the fees and charges paid or payable by that Party under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" with no "greater of ... USD 1,000,000" floor; the drafter expressly declined to propose the monetary floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Neither 21.3 nor any retained provision (21.1, 21.2, 4.9) excludes indirect, consequential, special or incidental damages; the margin comment concedes the consequential-damages exclusion was not volunteered.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 carves out "its breach of Paragraph 31" by bare number only; Paragraph 31 is not in the cited paragraphs, rendered language or resolved definitions, so the operative text does not itself show that the carve-out reaches confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The 21.3 carve-out list is limited to indemnification under 21.2, breach of Paragraph 31, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears.
21.3 opens "Except in respect of a Party's indemnification obligations under Subparagraph 21.2 ... which are not subject to any limit", placing the 21.2 cross-indemnity outside the new cap.
21.3 carve-out expressly includes "its gross negligence" among items "not subject to any limit".
No fraud carve-out in 21.3 or elsewhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears in 21.3; the carve-out list stops at wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 contains no statement that our payment obligations (contributions, fees and charges under the Agreement) are not "damages" subject to the cap, so the cap could be argued to swallow our own payment duties.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.3 applies to "each Party's aggregate liability to each other Party" — a single mutual cap, with no one-sided protection for any Party.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.3: cap equals "the fees and charges paid or payable by that Party under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee basis, above the 6-month walk-away floor.
21.3's opening exception covers "a Party's indemnification obligations under Subparagraph 21.2", so the cross-indemnity sits outside the new cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out is drafted as "its breach of Paragraph 31" without any descriptor; Paragraph 31's text is not supplied, so on the operative language alone it cannot be confirmed that the confidentiality obligations are the carved-out subject matter.
"its gross negligence" is listed in the 21.3 exception.
"its wilful misconduct" is listed in the 21.3 exception.

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct on the record: the Agreement (21.1 several liability, 21.2 Schedule B-limited cross-indemnity, 4.9 PG non-liability) contains no aggregate monetary cap and no consequential-damages exclusion, so our liability is unlimited in amount and the fallback is failed on a material term.

Fallback is not position-complete because the confidentiality carve-out is a bare numeric cross-reference. Repair in operative language: replace "its breach of Paragraph 31" with "its breach of its confidentiality obligations under Paragraph 31" so the carve-out is self-identifying and does not depend on an unverified paragraph number.

Intent failure: the words "which are not subject to any limit" contradict the retained, Customer-favourable proviso in 21.2 that "no indemnifying Party shall be obligated to contribute more than its share of liability as per Schedule B". Repair: scope the exception to this clause only — e.g. "...which are not subject to the limit set out in this Subparagraph 21.3" (or add "without prejudice to the Schedule B share limitation in Subparagraph 21.2") — so the Schedule B share ceiling survives intact.

Preferred level is not reached and is not required to be: no USD 1,000,000 floor, no mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or IP infringement, and no statement that our payment obligations are outside the capped "damages". These are noted as shortfalls from the preferred wording, not separate deviations.

Minimality is satisfied in structure: a single concise new Subparagraph 21.3 inserted where no cap existed, with no survival tail, expense language, procedures or extra damages categories, and no deletion of the favourable several-liability or Schedule B language.

Drafting note for the comment: it accurately states the fallback posture, but once the two repairs above are made the comment should also confirm that the Schedule B share limit in 21.2 is unaffected.
